problem.concept: the mining algorithm uses the same global criterion to decide whether a subgraph qualifies as a community. In other words, the criterion is fixed and predetermined. But in reality, communities for different vertices may have very different characteristics.
it is costly, time consuming, and often unnecessary to find communities for an entire network.
algorithms essentially materialize a snapshot of the overlapping communities in the network: the approach does not support dynamically evolving networks.

task.concept: predicting the guide strands of miRNAs

method.concept: mono-, di-, and tri-nucleotide composition of miRNA strands

contribution.concept: SVM models developed for predicting the guide strands of miRNAs
web server has been developed based on SVM models described in this study

SVM: dataset consisting of 329 miRNA and 329 miRNA* pairs using five fold cross validation technique: models were developed using mono-, di-, and tri-nucleotide composition of miRNA strands and achieved the highest accuracies of 0.588, 0.638 and 0.596 respectively.

SVM: dataset consisting of 329 miRNA and 329 miRNA* pairs using five fold cross validation technique: models were developed using split nucleotide composition and achieved maximum accuracies of 0.553, 0.641 and 0.602 for mono-, di-, and tri-nucleotide respectively.

SVM: dataset consisting of 329 miRNA and 329 miRNA* pairs using five fold cross validation technique: models were developed using binary pattern and achieved the highest accuracy of 0.708. Furthermore, when integrating the secondary structure features with binary pattern, an accuracy of 0.719 was seen.

SVM: dataset consisting of 329 miRNA and 329 miRNA* pairs using five fold cross validation technique: hybrid models were developed by combining various features and achieved maximum accuracy of 0.799 with sensitivity 0.781 and specificity 0.818. Moreover, the performance of this model was tested on an independent dataset that achieved an accuracy of 0.80.
guide and passenger strand of miRNA precursors can be distinguished using their nucleotide sequence and secondary structure.
